s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative corneal inflammation with deep stromal involvement
salient_findings: Keratitis in the right eye two months after DSAEK
Brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma
Central infiltrate involving all corneal layers on optical coherence tomography
key_facts: 68-year-old man with pseudophakic bullous keratopathy
Underwent DSAEK in the right eye
History of eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa 9 months before DSAEK
Postoperative course was initially uneventful under topical and systemic corticosteroids
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/200 in the right eye
Pupils were isocoric and isoreactive without an afferent pupillary defect
No pain with ocular movements
Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showed brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma
Anterior chamber was deep and clear
Intraocular pressure and fundus examination were normal

shortlist.label: Fungal keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma are consistent with fungal infection

shortlist.label: Acanthamoeba keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of contact lens use is not mentioned, but Acanthamoeba keratitis can occur in any corneal injury or infection

shortlist.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Keratitis with deep stromal involvement can be caused by herpes simplex virus

shortlist.label: Candida keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Fungal keratitis is a common complication of corneal surgery, and Candida is a common fungal pathogen

shortlist.label: Aspergillus keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Aspergillus is a common cause of fungal keratitis, especially in cases with a history of ocular trauma or surgery

raw.rationale: The presence of brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma, as seen on slit-lamp biomicroscopy, is consistent with fungal keratitis, particularly given the history of previous eye infection and the timing of the symptoms post-DSAEK.

rejected.label: Acanthamoeba keratitis
rejected.why: Typically associated with contact lens use and more severe pain, which is not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
rejected.why: Usually presents with dendritic ulcers and epithelial defects, not seen in this case

rejected.label: Candida keratitis
rejected.why: Less likely given the specific description of the lesions and the lack of other typical findings

rejected.label: Aspergillus keratitis
rejected.why: While possible, the description does not specifically point towards Aspergillus, and Fungal keratitis is a broader category that includes Aspergillus
